PROOF-1.case: the install block under step 1 of docs/getting-started.md against the one under "Install" in README.md; the proof says they are the same lines; the changed guide opens with `cd your-project` where the README has `cd my-project`

explanation: PROOF-1: the test reads the install lines of both pages through helpers, asserts the two lists are equal and that the only marketplace address in each is the ADDRESS constant, which is what the proof names.

PROOF-1: the helpers' source is not shown, so whether they keep every fenced line or only the `claude` lines is not visible; `assert len(readme) >= 2` would hold either way, and a difference in a line the helpers drop would still pass.
PROOF-1: the address is compared with a constant defined outside the test's own lines, so the test body does not itself show that it reads `https://github.com/rlabarca/purlin.git`.
PROOF-1: the last two assertions check the helper on a made-up page and a one-word difference built inside the test, and observe nothing further about the two real pages.

PROOF-2.case: the install commands of docs/getting-started.md run in an empty project with the address swapped for this checkout; the proof says `purlin@purlin` is installed and enabled for that project; the changed page's install command names a marketplace `rlabarca` that was never added, so the install fails a

explanation: PROOF-2: the test reads the plugin's row from the `installed` fixture and asserts it is enabled, has scope `project` and names the test's project folder, then asserts `claude plugin list` prints `purlin@purlin` and `enabled`, which is what the proof names.

PROOF-2: the `installed` fixture and `purlin_entry` are not shown, so it cannot be seen from the test whether the commands it runs are taken from every page or from one; a wrong command on a page the fixture does not read would still pass.

PROOF-2: the check `'enabled' in shown.stdout` reads the whole output and not the `purlin@purlin` row, so on its own another plugin's row could satisfy it; the row assertions above it cover the plugin's own state.
PROOF-2: the spot tests found nothing, and the test's assertions can each fail.

PROOF-3.case: the install of PROOF-2; the proof says the folder the installed plugin reads its skills from holds a SKILL.md for each folder under skills/ of the checkout, byte for byte; the changed manifest makes that folder docs/, which holds no SKILL.md for any skill

explanation: PROOF-3: the test finds the skills folder from the installed plugin's own manifest, checks it lies inside the installed plugin and exists, and compares the set of folders holding a `SKILL.md` there with the checkout's skill folders, so a missing or extra skill fails it.

PROOF-3: the test reads each installed `SKILL.md` and the checkout's as bytes and compares them for equality, which is the "same bytes" the proof names, with the expected bytes taken from the checkout's files and not from the installer.
PROOF-3: the test also asserts at least 9 skill folders, so an empty or short list of names in the checkout cannot pass it.
PROOF-3: the test checks what the proof names for the proof's own case, so the bug is the plainest one: the manifest names another folder as the one skills are read from.
PROOF-3: the rule says every skill is present word for word and the proof and test read only each skill's `SKILL.md`, so any other file inside a skill's folder is not compared.
Findings: the spot tests made none, and the test's assertions are each failable and compare against values the code under test does not produce.

PROOF-4.after:
name: drift
description: Report what a pull, a merge, a rebase or a checkout changed in the rules, the proofs and the tests, and name a number two branches both took
disable-model-invocation: true
PROOF-4.before:
name: drift
description: Report what a pull, a merge, a rebase or a checkout changed in the rules, the proofs and the tests, and name a number two branches both took
PROOF-4.case: after the install, the smallest model is asked to list the purlin: slash commands; the proof says its answer names every skill folder under skills/; the changed code keeps drift out of what the model is offered, so the answer does not name drift

explanation: PROOF-4: the test runs the one prompt in the installed project, requires exit 0 and an answer that is not an error, and then requires every folder name under skills/ to appear in the answer as a whole `purlin:` command name, which is the result the proof names.

PROOF-4: the expected names are read from the skill folders on disk and not from the model's answer, and a command is matched whole, so `purlin:spec-from-code` does not stand in for `spec` and a renamed skill does not stand in for its folder.
PROOF-4: the check that at least 9 folders are found stops an empty or short folder list from passing the comparison with nothing to compare.

PROOF-4: the test reads only the text of the answer, so a model that named a command it was not offered would still pass; nothing in the files shown gives the model that name by another route in the test's project.
PROOF-4: the spot tests made no finding, and the test leaves no way past it for a change that drops a skill from the answer, so the bug is the plain one.
notes: PROOF-4 rests on a single answer from a live model and carries no `@ai` tag, so one run decides it.

PROOF-5.case: the install made as the pages give it; the proof says the person's own installed plugins read the same before and after; the changed page installs purlin at user scope, so the person's own plugin list gains purlin

explanation: PROOF-5: the test reads the person's own plugins and marketplaces after the install and compares each with the reading taken before it, so a change to either list fails the test.
PROOF-5: the install itself is made in a fixture that is not shown, so whether it follows the README, docs/getting-started.md or both cannot be read from the test's own lines.
PROOF-5: the last assertion checks that the folder is gone straight after the test's own call deletes it, so it observes the test's cleanup and nothing the install did.
PROOF-5: the rule also names the person's own Claude Code settings, and the test compares only the plugin and marketplace lists, so a changed setting outside those two lists would pass.
Findings: none were made by the spot tests, and the test holds failable comparisons against values read before the install.
notes: PROOF-5 names the deletion of the test's project folder, which is the test's own mechanics and not something a user of the install would see.
